review.wirePersistenceRuntimeImpact: No wire-format change. Adds versioned profile ownership/selectors and opaque credential references, native protected secret storage, five Developer-gated Tauri commands, and the R8-kept Android credential JNI bridge. Mode changes serialize with identity/interface lifecycle, commit after readiness, retain unlocked identity only for same-profile rebuild, and verify rollback. External clients authenticate without fallback and reject local interface changes. New managed profiles are standalone; existing private sharing and operator selectors are preserved. AutoInterface UDP remains unchanged. Retains the previously reviewed announce/readiness boundaries and BLE firmware startup policy. Failed Link/packet recovery now uses the transport's bounded exact-attempt owner, with no ordinary receive-interface quarantine. Atomic packet receipts retain validated proofs across retry queues; canonical first-hop timing drives packet and Link deadlines, while bounded protocol clocks take precedence over orphan watchdogs. Packet RTT still reaches DB, UI events and Activity. No new UI setting, wire format, native dependency or Auto delivery policy change. Adds voice_set_talk with exact established Link and monotonic edge serials. Constrained Codec2 calls require renewed local input and retain their profile ceiling. Existing LXMF Ogg/Opus memos and wire IDs are unchanged. Adds standard LXMF audio mode 0x03 compact clips (15-second capture / 30-second receive), typed decode/record APIs and a defaulted audio_mode in existing IPC results. Runtime AudioMessageRequest now explicitly carries audio_mode. Schema 44 stores per-identity/destination format preferences; no capability guessing or new wire IDs. Stored playback resolves the mode from the identity-bound message row. Existing Opus recording, calls and ownership barriers are retained. October 8: recording selects native 700C only for explicit no-compression peer metadata from live/cache discovery, otherwise Opus; this is an application heuristic, not a new codec advertisement. Schema 44 preference rows remain readable but no longer control new recordings or send validation; the existing format IPC is read-only and rejects override arguments. The selected recording mode remains frozen. Retryable staged owners preserve cancellation authority and may restore only after definite pre-admission failure. Durable admission, lease transfer, canonical finalization and queue notification retain the originating identity lifecycle lock even if the IPC future is dropped. Asynchronous conversation broadcasts reject stale identity generations. Ambiguous queue completion never restores a sendable token. No dependency pin, manifest, wire mode, mobile bridge, runtime ceiling or MSRV change.
